title: DNS Service Binding RFC 9461 Client Policy and Registry Architecture
purpose: Define client and operator policy behavior plus registry constants for the remaining RFC 9461 DNS SVCB mapping requirements.
design_summary: The policy slice keeps RFC 9461 endpoint selection separate from endpoint use. `DnsServiceBindingClientPolicy` models dohpath HTTPS RR query suppression, secure transport authentication to the SVCB authentication name, DNS-query client identity suppression, invalid-response query suppression and optional logging, SVCB-reliant behavior after successful resolution, dependent-specification fallback adjustment, and cleartext fallback discouragement. `DnsServiceBindingOperatorGuidance` models equivalent HTTPS RR publication and speed-oriented AliasMode/TargetName guidance. `DnsServiceBindingRecord` exposes dohpath, SVCB RR type, port key, and automatic mandatory-port metadata.
data_and_state_considerations: The policy is immutable and side-effect free. It does not perform DNS resolution, open TLS/QUIC/HTTPS connections, emit logs, or publish DNS records.
edge_cases_and_constraints: DoH endpoints with dohpath do not query HTTPS RRs.
DNS-query client authentication remains disabled unless the endpoint is specifically known safe.
Invalid DNS responses suppress further queries and may be logged.
Cleartext fallback is disabled by default and can be adjusted only by dependent specification policy.
Registry constants are explicit for dohpath, SVCB RR type, and the automatically mandatory port key.
risks: This slice does not implement a DNS recursive resolver or SVCB RR wire parser.
This slice does not publish DNS records for operators.
This slice does not perform TLS certificate validation; it identifies the authentication name to use.

supplemental_sections.heading: Implementation Boundary
supplemental_sections.content: The client-policy boundary lets callers make RFC 9461 decisions around already-selected endpoints while keeping the DNS package independent from a concrete resolver loop or operator publication system.
